Follow-up retry investigation: hosted MCP read helpers already retry transient
network/HTTP failures up to three attempts within an eight-second budget, with
2.5-second attempt timeouts and exponential jitter. Java Supabase retries include
SQLSTATE `57014`, and catalog-reset lifecycle calls have their own 30-minute
retry window. The shared lifecycle poller also retries transient status failures.
The investigation found that `supaflow-app/src/lib/server/programmaticAccess.ts`
read the access policy once with a five-second fetch timeout before tool
execution. This gap was not proven to explain the observed 503s.

The requested follow-up is now implemented, uncommitted:

- The shared access-policy read uses the existing bounded read-retry helper.
  This benefits hosted MCP and CLI bootstrap, retains fresh authorization per
  admission, fails closed, and does not retry policy mutations or denials.
- CLI bootstrap retries transient HTTP/network failures up to three attempts
  within 30 seconds, with a 15-second attempt limit, backoff/jitter, and
  Retry-After handling. It does not replay the CLI command or expose response
  bodies in errors.
- Java reset COMMIT/ABORT diagnostics include the phase, exception class, HTTP
  status, and a format-validated database code. Raw error messages, reasons,
  response bodies, and stack traces are excluded from these diagnostics.
